'''Alen Smailagić''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Ален Смаилагић}}, born August 18, 2000) is a Serbian professional basketball player who currently plays for the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].

Samalagić is the youngest player in history to play in the [[NBA G League]].<ref name="bluemanhoop">{{cite web |title=Golden State Warriors: Analyzing Alen Smailagić, the newest G-League addition |url=https://bluemanhoop.com/2018/11/01/golden-state-warriors-alen-smailagic-draft/ |website=bluemanhoop.com |accessdate=19 March 2019}}</ref>

== Early career ==
Samalagić started to play basketball for [[KK Beko|Beko]] in [[Belgrade]]. In 2012, he joined their youth teams. In the 2017–18 season, Samalagić played for Beko in Junior Serbian League and averaged 21.7 points, 11.1 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game over 19 games.<ref name="serbiahoop">{{cite web|title=Focus on: Alen Smailagić |url=http://www.serbiahoop.com/focus-on-alen-smailagic/|website=serbiahoop.com|accessdate=19 March 2019}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Samalagić made his senior debut for [[KK Beko|Beko]] of the semi-professional [[Serbian basketball league system|3rd-tier]] [[First Regional Basketball League (Serbia)|Serbian Regional League]] in the 2017–18 season. Over ten league games, he averaged 15.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game.<ref name="serbiahoop"/><ref name="bluemanhoop"/>

On October 20, 2018, Smajlagić was selected as the 4th pick on the [[2018 NBA G League draft]] by the [[South Bay Lakers]], but he was traded right away to the [[Golden State Warriors]] affiliate, [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], which makes him the youngest player in the history of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alen Smailagic Is The Warriors' Draft Target They Don't Want You To Know About... Yet|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jefffeld/2018/12/27/alen-smailagic-is-the-warriors-draft-target-they-dont-want-you-to-know-about-yet/#c6db0b55d858|website=forbes.com|accessdate=19 March 2019}}</ref> Smajlagić made his debut for the Warriors on November 3, 2018, scoring 3 points in 7 minutes he spent on the court.<ref name="bluemanhoop"/>

== National team career ==
Smajlagić was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-16 basketball team|Serbian under-16 national team]] that competed at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 5.0 points, 5.7 rebounds and 0.3 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Serbia 11 - Alen Smailagic |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/131821/sid/12295/tid/96799/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U16_European_Championship/index.html |website=archive.fiba.com |accessdate=19 March 2019}}</ref>
